description:
Title: Forecasted plateau autoscaler and utilization telemetry proxy

Motivation and summary: Dedicated capacity customers experience frequent small oscillations in scale decisions when traffic hovers near a capacity breakpoint (short-lived plateaus). This PR introduces a forecast-driven plateau detector and a lightweight telemetry proxy that aggregates cross-cluster utilization signals to produce a more confident, stable scaling decision. The goal is to reduce thrashing during short plateau periods while preserving fast scale-up for true demand spikes.

What this changes (high level):
- New plateau detector that scores a short forecast window (configurable 30s-5m) and computes a "plateau_score" (0..1) using an EWMA over recent derivative and variance of token throughput.
- Decision engine wraps existing autoscaler: when plateau_score > threshold and forecast indicates stable plateau, the autoscaler applies a conservative ramp (soft-increment) and extends scale-down grace to avoid premature shrink.
- Telemetry proxy service aggregates per-tenant 50/90/95/99 token throughput percentiles and in-flight KV-cache hit ratios across local clusters, exposing util.cross_cluster_util_proxy and util.plateau_score metrics for the autoscaler to consume. Proxy uses sampling and categorical bloom to bound memory.
- Feature flag gating (feature.autoscaler.plateau) and chart values to control rollout. Canary configuration included.
- New e2e and integration tests plus perf-canary harness scenario that simulates plateau traffic patterns.
- Console dashboards and docs updated with suggested thresholds and operational playbook.

Design notes and rationale:
- We intentionally avoid large global locks or synchronous cross-region pulls. The proxy emits summarized, time-bucketed metrics; the controller treats those as advisory signals and will fall back to local metrics if proxy data is stale.
- Hysteresis: plateau_score adds a time-decay; scale-down is gated by both time and plateau confidence to minimize user-facing latency regressions caused by oscillation.
- Safety: all changes are behind a feature flag and default to off for existing customers. The autoscaler still respects reservation commitments and tenant-level minima.

Testing and CI:
- Unit coverage added for plateau detector and forecast window sampling.
- Integration tests run with a synthetic plateau workload in the perf-canary cluster (integration/canary/plateau_canary.yaml).
- One flaky e2e test (e2e/plateau_autoscaler_test.go::TestCanaryPlateauRamp) failed on first CI run due to timing variability; we tightened timing assertions and reran. Final CI: 1 failed (flake) then 2nd run passed; all checks green.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/autoscaler/*: new detector and decision wiring, feature-flag checks.
- pkg/telemetry/proxy/*: proxy aggregator and HTTP metrics endpoint with bounded memory.
- api/metrics/v1: lightweight endpoint and schema for plateau_score and cross_cluster util.
- charts/dedicated: values to enable canary and default thresholds.
- e2e/integration: tests to validate non-regressive behaviour under plateau.
- docs: ops runbook, recommended thresholds, and troubleshooting steps.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Aisha Nuru (reviewer): "Nice direction — please confirm that the proxy cannot be used as a hard source of truth. We should cap the influence of cross-cluster signals to X% to avoid misattribution."
- Miguel (author): "Agree — capped influence is implemented in decision_engine.go as 'proxy_influence_pct' (default 25%). I'll add comments and an integration test asserting fallbacks when proxy goes stale."
- Luca Romano (reviewer): "Can we avoid blocking scale-up paths under low confidence? A note about fast path for emergency scale-up would help."
- Miguel (author): "Implemented: when forecast confidence < 0.4 but instantaneous local util > high_watermark, autoscaler takes fast-path scale-up. Documented in ops runbook and added unit tests."
- Harper Li (reviewer): "Tests look good; please add console panel for plateau_score and ensure telemetry retention is bounded."
- Miguel (author): "Added plateau_score panel and retention note in docs; proxy uses fixed bucket retention by default."

Deployment and rollout:
- Feature flag default OFF. Canary rollout plan: enable on 10% of Dedicated fleets for 48 hours with a traffic shadowing period; monitor util.plateau_score and tail latencies.
- If plateau_score consistently > 0.7 with reduced scale churn and no P99 tail regressions, expand to 50% then 100% over 7 calendar days.
- Rollback plan: disable feature flag and quickly revert canary chart; autoscaler will immediately revert to baseline behavior.

Operational notes:
- New metrics to watch: util.plateau_score, util.cross_cluster_util_proxy, autoscaler.proxy_influence_pct_used, autoscaler.plateau_decisions_count.
- Recommended defaults in docs: plateau_threshold=0.6, forecast_window=60s, proxy_influence_pct=25%.

Release notes: 
- Added forecasted-plateau autoscaler to reduce scale thrash during short demand plateaus (off by default).
- Introduced telemetry proxy for aggregated cross-cluster utilization signals.

Backwards compatibility:
- No breaking API changes. Proxy exposes optional metrics; controllers fallback to local metrics if unavailable.

Merge: squash merged into main after approvals from Aisha, Luca, and Harper.

release_notes: Forecasted plateau autoscaler (off by default) — reduces scale thrash by detecting short-lived plateaus and applying conservative scaling decisions.
Telemetry proxy — optional aggregation layer exposing cross_cluster util signals for better scaling confidence.
Canary rollout and feature flag included.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report sudden capacity regressions after enabling, disable feature.autoscaler.plateau and check autoscaler.proxy_influence_pct_used metric; if proxy reports stale buckets, revert immediately and investigate proxy aggregator memory pressure.
